title: Verification, certification, and why time of death is not the witness’s burden

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: A witness thinks the person has died, but the official processes—verifying death, certifying death, recording details, and registering—belong to trained people and local systems.
ordinary_language_queries: time of death hospice at home
professional_terms: medical certificate of cause of death

content_layers.observation_text: Public sources distinguish the human recognition that someone has died from formal verification, certification, death-certificate, and registration processes.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Marie Curie and Macmillan supply after-death process language; the archive should use them to prevent lay witness records from becoming pronouncement or legal paperwork guides.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: The witness may remember the last breath, but official time and certification are not theirs to carry. This record is a burden-removal record.

what_this_is_not: not a universal description of who can verify or certify
not a claim that the witness must know the exact minute
uncertainties: Professional roles and legal language vary by jurisdiction.
Hospital, hospice, care home, coroner/medical examiner, and home-death pathways differ.
Organ donation, autopsy, custody death, or unexplained death requires separate treatment.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should separate “I think they died” from “someone official verifies/certifies,” reducing panic around exact timing.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect plain-language explanations of verification, certification, registration, and what families actually need to do next.
language_notes: Use “verification” and “certification” only with definitions and local caveat.
Avoid using “pronouncement” as if it is universal.
Do not make exact time of death into moral performance.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
